blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: Let's name our cat Cookie.
exercises.why: **назвать → назовём** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future. Давай — one person (ты); Давайте — several people, or one person by вы; the verb is the same.

exercises.prompt: I'll repeat the most important ideas.
exercises.why: **повторить → повторю** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Please connect a controller.
exercises.why: **подключить → подключите** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Можешь говорить до посинения, ты всё равно меня не ___ (убедить).
exercises.prompt: You can talk until you're blue in the face, but you'll never convince me.
exercises.why: **убедить → убедишь** — perfective verb, 2nd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Давайте ___ (устроить) побудку по телефону в семь утра.
exercises.prompt: Let's arrange for a 7:00 a.m. wake-up call.
exercises.why: **устроить → устроим** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future. Давай — one person (ты); Давайте — several people, or one person by вы; the verb is the same.

exercises.prompt: Just compare the facts.
exercises.why: **сравнить → сравните** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Большинство иностранцев никогда в полной мере не ___ (освоить) немецкие модальные частицы.
exercises.prompt: Most foreigners will never fully master the use of German modal particles.
exercises.why: **освоить → освоит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Apply a cold compress to the affected area.
exercises.why: **приложить → Приложите** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Много средств ___ (уйти) на обустройство новой квартиры.
exercises.prompt: It costs a lot to furnish a new apartment.
exercises.why: **уйти → уйдёт** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Cut all the fat from the meat.
exercises.why: **удалить → Удалите** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: The candle of my life will go out soon.
exercises.why: **потухнуть → потухнет** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Если дамба ___ (обрушиться), тысячи людей могут погибнуть.
exercises.prompt: Thousands of people could be killed if the dam fails.
exercises.why: **обрушиться → обрушится** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: I will leave tomorrow, in any event.
exercises.why: **уехать → уеду** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Food will attract bears.
exercises.why: **привлечь → привлечёт** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: I will sleep at ten o'clock.
exercises.why: **уснуть → усну** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Будешь продолжать в том же духе - они тебя в психушку ___ (отправить).
exercises.prompt: If you carry on like this, they'll send you to the loony bin.
exercises.why: **отправить → отправят** — perfective verb, 3rd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Who'll pay for the loss?
exercises.why: **заплатить → заплатит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: We will survive with God's help!
exercises.why: **спастись → Спасёмся** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Lean your head forward.
exercises.why: **наклонить → Наклоните** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Я знал, что с Томом проблем не ___ (обобраться).
exercises.prompt: I knew Tom was a troublemaker.
exercises.why: **обобраться → оберёшься** — perfective verb, 2nd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
